main_body: Green tile hip roof (rows 4-42) over a cream shrine wall with red pillars, a red lintel beam and a lattice double door, on a grey stone base
top_band: Ridge cap at rows 4-8 in light and mid green (L 168/138/88), with gold ridge ornaments above at rows 0-3. Below it the roof slope is a tapering trapezoid of green tiles at rows 10-41, ending in a light eave row at rows 42-43.
evidence: At x=71 the column runs ridge cap (rows 4-9), then roof slope (rows 10-41), then a light eave row (rows 42-43), then a red lintel beam (rows 44-46), then the wall and door face (rows 47-72), then the stone base. The roof slope is a large tapered surface seen from above, like the reference house roofs, so a horizontal surface is clearly visible over a distinct front face. The light eave row is the front-edge line, and the dark red lintel under it works as the eave shadow. The lattice door sits inset between the pillars, with darker inner tones. No receding side faces are drawn.

style.evidence: The roof has about 5 green steps, but the tile pattern is a mechanical grid of identical rectangles with no per-tile scallops or variation, unlike the reference tile roofs. The cream wall panels are large and nearly flat, with only sparse speckle. The dark edge pixels are 83% neutral (e.g. #231d28 on the roof silhouette), against 7-9% in the references, so the outline reads as a near-black sticker line rather than a dark tone of the adjacent material. The piece has only 32 distinct colours, against 66 and 185 in the references. Median colours per tile (11) match the stone reference, but the overall palette and the outline are shallower than the Beodeul standard.
